blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
A UK email is short, polite and clear. You don't need to write a speech. You just need the right opener, a clear body, and the correct sign-off.

Start with "Dear" when the email is formal. Use "Hi" only with colleagues you already know. After that, write one warm line, and then go straight to your point. Keep the body short. One topic per email is best.

At the end, close with "Best regards" or "Kind regards". Always re-read your email before you send it. In the UK, a short email is not rude — it is a sign of respect for the reader's time.

items.q: According to the text, how should a UK email be?
items.why: "A UK email is short, polite and clear."

items.q: When should you use "Dear"?
items.why: "Start with 'Dear' when the email is formal."

items.q: How many topics should one email have?
items.why: "One topic per email is best."

items.q: The text suggests that a short email in the UK is…
items.why: Inferência: "a short email is not rude — it is a sign of respect".

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: A longer email is always more polite.
A good email goes straight to the point.
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende emails curtos, então a ideia de que "quanto mais longo, mais educado" contraria o autor.

blocks.instruction: Ouça o colaborador falando sobre o seu primeiro email para Londres. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Today I sent my first email to a colleague in London. Her name is Emma, and we work on the same project. I was a little nervous, so I read the tips again before I started.

First, I chose a clear subject line: "Project update — Tuesday". Then I opened with "Dear Emma". I wrote one warm line, and after that I went straight to my point. I only wrote about one topic, so it was easy to read.

The email was short — just four lines. I said what I needed, I said thank you, and I closed with "Best regards". Before sending, I read it two times to check for mistakes.

Emma replied in ten minutes. She said thank you, and she answered my question. Her email was short too — even shorter than mine! Now I feel more confident. A good email in the UK is not long. It is clear and polite, and it respects the other person's time.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Who did the speaker write to?
options: A colleague in London named Emma
items.why: "I sent my first email to a colleague in London. Her name is Emma."

items.q: How did the speaker open the email?
items.why: "Then I opened with 'Dear Emma'."

items.q: What did the speaker do before sending the email?
options: He asked a colleague to check it
He read it two times to check for mistakes
items.why: "Before sending, I read it two times to check for mistakes."

items.q: How did the speaker feel at the end?
items.why: Inferência: "Now I feel more confident" — a experiência correu bem.

items.q: What can we understand from Emma's reply?
options: She was upset by the short email
She did not understand the message
Short, clear emails work well in the UK
items.why: Inferência: ela respondeu em 10 minutos, agradeceu e foi ainda mais curta — o estilo curto funciona.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Please open every email with a polite line." An email is…
items.why: Email = mensagem enviada pela internet.

items.q: "Dear Mr Brown, thank you for your time." We use "Dear" to…
items.why: "Dear" = abertura formal (Prezado).

items.q: Choose the correct word: "I closed the email with "Best ___"."
items.why: "Best regards" = atenciosamente, fechamento neutro.

items.q: "Her email had a clear subject: 'Meeting on Friday'." The subject is…
options: the topic line at the top
items.why: Subject = assunto, a linha do topo que diz o tema.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "I sent my question in the morning and got a fast ___."
items.why: Reply = resposta a um email.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em emails de trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "I will get back to you tomorrow." This means I will…
items.why: Get back to someone = responder/dar retorno depois.

items.q: "Can you follow up with Emma about the report?" To follow up means to…
options: check again and continue the topic
items.why: Follow up = dar continuidade, cobrar/verificar depois.

items.q: "Feel free to reach out if you have questions." This means you can…
items.why: Reach out = entrar em contato, procurar alguém.

items.q: "The manager needs to sign off on the email before we send it." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Just drop me a line when the file is ready." This means…
items.why: Drop someone a line = mandar uma mensagem rápida.
